implementation_notes: The BCL supplies the queue: ConcurrentQueue<T> is a thread-safe FIFO whose TryEnqueue/TryDequeue let an owner thread drain per frame, BlockingCollection<T> adds blocking and bounded semantics, and System.Threading.Channels.Channel<T> is the async twin whose WaitToReadAsync/ReadAllAsync replaces a condition variable for pipelines. What replaces the classic structure is these types plus one owner thread that decides when to drain; the classic hand-written queue is still justified when the events must be coalesced or inspected as a batch, which the BCL types do not express.
pitfalls: ConcurrentQueue<T>.Count walks the segment list and is O(n): poll IsEmpty (or keep your own atomic counter) instead of Count in a hot loop.
The collection is thread-safe but the handler is not: drained events must be processed on one owner thread or the handler needs its own synchronization.
Deferred events capture object references: a dead entity's graph can be mutated or disposed before the drain, so snapshot the payload instead of looking the world up later.
